input: FoolWidget Inc. announced today its Q3 earnings, reporting revenue of $42.3M, up 18% year over year. CEO Maria Chen said the growth was driven by a 31% increase in enterprise subscriptions, particularly in the EMEA region. The company added 1,247 new enterprise customers, bringing the total to 8,902. Operating margin improved from 12% to 17%. Chen highlighted that the Pro plan, launched in May, now accounts for 23% of revenue. She did not provide guidance for Q4 but said the company expects 'continued momentum' through the holiday quarter.

Researchers at MIT published a paper in Nature on Tuesday describing a new approach to lithium-ion battery design that could increase energy density by 35%. The team, led by Dr. Anwar Hossain, used a silicon-graphite composite anode and a novel electrolyte formulation. Lab prototypes achieved 412 Wh/kg, compared to ~300 Wh/kg for current commercial cells. The paper notes the prototype maintains 92% capacity after 1,000 charge cycles. Commercialization is at least 4-5 years away, the team estimates. The research was funded by the U.S. Department of Energy and a consortium of three automakers.

The European Commission today proposed a 12% tariff on imported electric scooters from a list of 14 countries, citing 'predatory pricing' that has reduced EU manufacturers' market share from 38% in 2022 to 19% in 2026. The tariff would take effect January 1, 2027 if approved by the Council. Industry group EuroMobility supported the move; consumer advocacy group BUREAU criticized it, estimating the tariff would add €120-180 to the average scooter price. Affected countries include China, Vietnam, India, and Turkey.

Mayor Lillian Park announced Friday that the city of Brookville will install 4,200 new EV charging ports over the next three years, funded by a $48M federal grant. Park said the goal is to ensure every resident lives within 800 meters of a charger by the end of 2029. Critics including councilmember Ahmed Rahman argued the project prioritizes affluent neighborhoods. The plan calls for 35% of chargers to be located in underserved zones. Construction is scheduled to begin in March.

Apple Inc. reported quarterly revenue of $94.9 billion, up 5% year over year, driven by services revenue of $24.6 billion (up 12%) and an installed base of over 2.2 billion active devices. iPhone revenue was $46 billion, roughly flat. China revenue declined 8%. CFO Luca Maestri said the company expects similar growth in Q1 2027 and gave guidance of 4-6% revenue growth. Apple announced a $90 billion share buyback program.

A new climate study from Stanford University, published Wednesday in Science, projects that global average temperature will rise 2.1-2.6°C above pre-industrial levels by 2080 under current emissions policies. The study, led by Dr. Elena Vasquez, used 47 climate models and incorporates new data on Arctic permafrost methane emissions. The lower bound is 0.3°C higher than the IPCC's 2024 assessment. Vasquez said meeting the 1.5°C target now appears 'effectively impossible' without aggressive carbon capture deployment, which currently stands at less than 0.1% of required scale.

GitHub announced Tuesday that it has acquired developer-tools startup Voltaic for an undisclosed sum, reportedly between $180M and $230M. Voltaic, founded in 2023, makes a code-review automation tool used by ~3,000 engineering teams. CEO Diana Rasmussen will join GitHub as VP of AI-assisted development. The product will be integrated into GitHub Copilot over the next 6 months and offered as part of the Enterprise tier. Voltaic's 47 employees will all join GitHub.

The London Borough of Hackney's transport committee voted 7-2 on Monday to remove 1.4 km of segregated cycle lanes on Kingsland Road, citing congestion concerns. The lanes were installed in 2021 at a cost of £2.8M. Cycling advocacy group Cyclists in the City said the decision was 'short-sighted' and noted that cycle traffic on Kingsland Road increased 67% between 2021 and 2025. The committee said replacement bus lanes would be installed in their place. Removal work begins in October.
